chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Abī Zāhir, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Abū Isḥāq al-Naḥwī, who said:
I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), and I heard him saying: “Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disciplined His Prophet upon His love,”
so He said: “And indeed you are surely upon a magnificent character.”
so the Mighty and Majestic said: “Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.”
And the Mighty and Majestic said: “Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah.”

He said: Then he said: “And indeed the Prophet of Allah delegated to ʿAlī and entrusted him. So you submitted, while the people denied. By Allah, we love that you speak when we speak, and that you remain silent when we remain silent. We are in that which is between you and Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah has not placed any good for anyone in opposing our command.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: “I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying,” then he mentioned something similar to it.

key_terms.أَدَّبَ: disciplined and refined in the highest moral and spiritual sense
key_terms.أَمْرِنَا: our command; the authoritative directive of the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.مَحَبَّتِهِ: His love; divine love as the basis of the Prophet’s formation

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain Allah’s delegation of authority to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, perfected the character of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and delegated authority to him in the matter of religion, as affirmed by Qur’anic verses commanding obedience to the Messenger. It then states that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم entrusted this authority to ʿAlī عليه السلام, emphasizing that goodness lies in conforming to the command of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and not opposing them.
